title: Repair Streaming Pipeline Anomaly Detector
objective: Fix StreamingAnomalyDetector in /app/detector/streaming.py to implement online statistical anomaly detection: per-stream EMA baselines via ema.py, pre-update z-scoring with effective_std, warmup gating, consecutive_required debouncing for false-positive control, and concept-drift responsiveness through ema_alpha. Only streaming.py may be edited. Done means passing visible self-check tests plus sealed hidden suites that verify FP rate, detection sensitivity, drift behavior, and full statistical equality against a hidden spec reference on unpublished streams.
motivation: Production ML-ops pipelines use online statistical detectors (EMA + z-score) to flag streaming metric anomalies while controlling false positives and adapting to concept drift. Broken detectors miss incidents or page on every spike. This task mirrors tuning a real detector module in an observability platform.
difficultyExplanation: Five interacting statistical rules: per-stream EMA state, pre-update z-scoring, warmup suppression, consecutive debouncing, and ema_alpha drift adaptation. The seed uses cumulative mean, wrong z denominator, global state, and immediate alerting. Hidden sealed tests include 50-point benign Gaussian FP checks (must be 0 alerts), sustained-attack sensitivity on wh_stat_* streams, alpha-trajectory checks proving EMA is used, manual z-score verification against ema.z_score, and full equality vs spec_reference.py — hard-coded or rule-based stubs cannot pass.
environmentSummary: Python 3.11 container, /app/detector/ with broken streaming.py and correct ema.py statistical helpers. Offline, no GPU. Agent reads instruction.md and patches streaming.py. Sealed /tests/ contains visible (documented) and hidden (statistical, behavioral, spec-reference) pytest modules the agent cannot read at runtime.

networkRequirements.justification: Fully offline statistical ML task; dependencies baked into Docker image.

oracleStrategy: solution/solve.sh installs reference streaming.py using ema.ema_update, ema.z_score, ema.effective_std with per-stream state, pre-update scoring, warmup/consecutive gating. Runs all four pytest modules (visible + 3 hidden layers) before grading.
verificationStrategy: Four-layer sealed verifier documented in VERIFICATION.md: (1) test_visible.py — 5 self-check cases in instruction.md; (2) test_hidden.py — stream isolation, 40-point benign FP=0, drift, spec-reference parametrized wh_unseen_* streams; (3) test_behavior_hidden.py — consecutive reset, min_std, alpha adaptation properties; (4) test_statistical_hidden.py — 50-point benign FP=0, sustained-attack sensitivity, z-score matches ema.z_score pre-update, alpha trajectory divergence, wh_stat_m* spec matrix. spec_reference.py provides canonical statistical implementation. invariants.py enforces warmup and anomaly consistency. Agent cannot read /tests/. Binary scoring.
binarySuccessCondition: All pytest cases in test_visible.py, test_hidden.py, test_behavior_hidden.py, and test_statistical_hidden.py pass when importing StreamingAnomalyDetector from /app/detector/streaming.py.
partialScoreStrategy: Binary only — prevents passing visible spike literals while failing sealed FP-rate and statistical-equality hidden tests.
anticipatedExploits: 1. Hard-coded is_anomaly responses — Prevention: sealed spec_reference equality on wh_unseen_* and wh_stat_m* streams requiring exact z-scores. 2. Rule-based if value > X — Prevention: 50-point benign Gaussian FP test must yield zero alerts. 3. Ignoring ema_alpha / cumulative mean — Prevention: alpha-trajectory test and post-drift baseline bounds. 4. Wrong z denominator (abs(mean)) — Prevention: statistical test verifies z matches ema.z_score on pre-update baseline; baseline_std != abs(mean) property test. 5. Single-point alerting — Prevention: consecutive_required and sustained-attack sensitivity test. 6. Global stream state — Prevention: stream isolation hidden test. 7. Skipping warmup — Prevention: invariants never-alert-before-warmup on every result. 8. Random anomaly flags — Prevention: deterministic sequences with exact expected statistical outputs.
